findings.evidence: InvariantMass.lean:104-108 `private theorem spatialPart_add_target (hq' : q.spatialPart = a • n) (hP' : P.spatialPart = -p • n) : (q + P).spatialPart = (a - p) • n := by rw [spatialPart_add, hq', hP', sub_smul, _root_.neg_smul, ← sub_eq_add_neg]`; all lemmas it is fed to are public in MinkowskiProductExtensions.lean:70,78,92,101 and take exactly the `spatialPart = a • n` hypothesis shape.
findings.fix: Move it public to `MinkowskiProductExtensions.lean` next to `minkowskiProduct_self_eq_mul_of_spatialPart_eq_smul`, with a neutral name (e.g. `spatialPart_add_eq_smul_of_spatialPart_eq_smul`) and no `_target` in it. `timeComponent_add_target` (line 98) is the same shape but carries nothing beyond the already-public `timeComponent_add`; inline it rather than exporting a near-duplicate.
findings.issue: `private theorem spatialPart_add_target` states `(q+P).spatialPart = (a - p) • n` from `q.spatialPart = a • n` and `P.spatialPart = -p • n`. Its statement mentions only `Lorentz.Vector d`, `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)` and `ℝ`, and its proof is `spatial_add`/`sub_smul`/`neg_smul` — no photoproduction content. It is the closure property (sum of collinear vectors is collinear) that the whole `_of_spatialPart_eq_smul` family added by this PR needs, yet no consumer outside this file can use it.

findings.evidence: Declaration list of InvariantMass.lean: the `CollinearPhoton` section holds only `exp_two_mul_rapidity_of_collinearPhoton` (:125), `photonEnergy_add_photonMomentum_add_targetEnergy_sub_momentum_eq_sqrt_mul_exp_rapidity` (:136) and `sqrt_minkowskiProduct_add_self_pos_of_collinearPhoton` (:146); Rapidity.lean:174 and :185 supply both signs upstream, so only the applied side is asymmetric.
findings.fix: Add the collinear backward component in the same section, via `timeComponent_sub_eq_sqrt_minkowskiProduct_mul_exp_neg_rapidity_of_spatialPart_eq_smul` (the upstream dual already proved in Rapidity.lean:185), and derive `targetEnergy_add_momentum_eq_sqrt_mul_exp_neg_rapidity` from it as the `a = k` case.
findings.issue: The `CollinearPhoton` section (any virtuality — the case the PR argues is the physical one, since `ChargedSource.not_isReal_of_mem_photonRegion` rules out real photons) exposes only the forward light-cone component `k + a + E - p = W e^{y}`. The dual `k - a + E + p = W e^{-y}` exists only in the real-photon specialisation (`targetEnergy_add_momentum_eq_sqrt_mul_exp_neg_rapidity`, line 180, which requires `q.spatialPart = k • n`). A consumer at nonzero virtuality cannot obtain it without re-proving `spatialPart_add_target`, which is private.

summary: The closure fact that a sum of two collinear four-vectors is collinear is hidden as a private photoproduction helper instead of living public beside the rest of the `_of_spatialPart_eq_smul` API, and the collinear (any-virtuality) section exposes only the forward light-cone component, so the backward one cannot be reconstructed by a consumer.
